seoTitle: Severance Test: Which Character Are You? (11 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the Severance test: 11 everyday questions reveal whether you're Mark, Helly, Dylan, Irving, Cobel, Milchick, Devon or Ricken — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the one keeping your head down, the rebel, or the rule-keeper who knows the handbook by heart? Answer 11 everyday questions about work, rules and secrets, and find out which Severance character you are.

characters.name: Mark S.
characters.title: The Reluctant Leader
characters.summary: Decent, steady and quietly carrying a lot. You keep your head down, until something finally makes you look up.
description: Like Mark, you keep your head down. He's a former history professor who now works in Lumon's Macrodata Refinement department.
You end up in charge, whether you like it or not. Mark becomes head of his department after his friend Petey leaves.
You'd rather not think about the hard stuff. Mark had his memories split so he could get through the workday without his grief.
characters.flaw: You go along with things for far too long before you push back.
characters.signature: A desk, a screen full of numbers and a feeling that something isn't right.
characters.clashReason: they'd go quiet and avoid the conversation

characters.name: Helly R.
characters.title: The Rebel
characters.summary: Brave, defiant and impossible to control. You don't follow orders you don't believe in, and you're always looking for the way out.
description: Like Helly, you don't follow orders blindly. She's the rebellious new hire in Mark's department.
You don't give up. Helly keeps trying to resign, even after her request is turned down.
You ask the questions nobody else will. From her very first day, Helly pushes back against Lumon's rules.
characters.flaw: You'd rather fight than wait, even when waiting is smarter.
characters.signature: A raised hand, a hard question and an escape plan.
characters.clashReason: they'd question every single thing you tell them

characters.name: Dylan G.
characters.title: The Competitor
characters.summary: Funny, competitive and always after the next prize. You want to be rewarded, and you'll let everyone know when you are.
description: Like Dylan, you love a reward. He's one of Mark's colleagues, and he particularly enjoys company perks.
You're quick with a comeback. Dylan is known for his sarcastic sense of humour.
You've got a temper when you're pushed. In season 1, Dylan goes for Milchick and has to be held back by his coworkers.
characters.flaw: You care a bit too much about who's winning.
characters.signature: A trophy shelf, a sarcastic comment and one eye on the next prize.
characters.clashReason: they'd turn everything into a competition, and gloat when they won

characters.name: Irving B.
characters.title: The Rule-Keeper
characters.summary: Loyal, principled and devoted to doing things properly. You know the rules inside out, and you have a romantic heart.
description: Like Irving, you know the rules inside out. He's Mark's colleague, and a stickler for company policy.
You're a romantic at heart. Irving falls for Burt, a colleague from another department.
You start asking questions, eventually. Despite his devotion to company policy, Irving begins to doubt Lumon.
characters.flaw: You trust the rules a little too much.
characters.signature: A spotless desk, a well-thumbed handbook and a rule for every occasion.
characters.clashReason: they'd correct you, politely, by quoting the handbook

characters.name: Harmony Cobel
characters.title: The Boss
characters.summary: Driven, devoted and always watching. You believe in the mission completely, and you don't let anything slip past you.
description: Like Cobel, you like to be in control. She's the manager of the severed floor at Lumon.
You believe in the mission. Cobel is deeply devoted to the philosophy of Kier Eagan, Lumon's founder.
You keep a close eye on people. Cobel keeps very close tabs on Mark.
characters.flaw: You can't let go, even when you really should.
characters.signature: A watchful eye, a firm rule and a plan nobody else knows about.
characters.clashReason: they'd watch your every move, and tell you it's for your own good

characters.name: Seth Milchick
characters.title: The Smooth Operator
characters.summary: Polished, composed and always professional. You keep everyone in line with a smile, and nobody quite knows what you're thinking.
description: Like Milchick, you're polished and always professional. He's the deputy manager on Lumon's severed floor.
You know how to reward people. Milchick hands out perks like the Music Dance Experience.
You keep everyone in line, with a smile. Milchick keeps Mark's team on a tight leash, always politely.
characters.flaw: You smile through everything, so nobody knows what you're really thinking.
characters.signature: A perfect smile, a calm voice and a reward for good behaviour.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you off with a smile, which is somehow worse

characters.name: Devon
characters.title: The Straight Talker
characters.summary: Honest, grounded and protective of the people you love. You say what everyone else is thinking, and you don't trust anything that sounds too good to be true.
description: Like Devon, you say it how it is. She's Mark's sister, and she's sceptical of Lumon and its severance procedure.
You look out for the people you love. Devon helps Mark through the ups and downs of his life.
You've got a lot going on. Devon gives birth to a baby in season 1.
characters.flaw: You push, even when someone isn't ready to hear it.
characters.signature: A straight answer, a sceptical look and a lot of patience.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you what they really think, whether you asked or not

characters.name: Ricken
characters.title: The Thinker
characters.summary: Thoughtful, curious and full of big ideas. You love a deep conversation, and you mean well, even when you get carried away.
description: Like Ricken, you love a big idea. He's Devon's husband, and an eccentric self-help author.
Your words go further than you think. Ricken's book, The You You Are, ends up inspiring Mark's team at work.
You get noticed. In season 2, Lumon wants to adapt Ricken's book for its severed workers.
characters.flaw: You talk about life so much that you sometimes forget to listen.
characters.signature: A notebook full of big thoughts and a book you think everyone should read.
characters.clashReason: they'd turn every chat into a lecture about the meaning of life

questions.text: It's your first day at a new job, and you're handed a thick rulebook. You...

options.text: Read it cover to cover, and remember all of it
Ask why half these rules even exist
Flip straight to the section on perks
Skim it, and keep your head down

questions.text: Your boss asks how you're doing. You...

options.text: Say you're fine, whatever's really going on
Smile, and say everything's wonderful
Tell them honestly. They did ask
Turn it into a deep conversation about what it means to be happy

questions.text: Your ideal Friday night looks like...

options.text: Games night, and you're not losing
Hosting a dinner party for everyone you know
A quiet night in, doing something you love
Something spontaneous. Rules are for weekdays

questions.text: A coworker breaks a small rule. You...

options.text: Pretend you didn't see it
Have a quiet, friendly word they won't forget
Help them get away with it
Make a note of it, and keep a close eye on them

questions.text: You're asked to do something at work that feels wrong. You...

options.text: Refuse, loudly, and tell everyone why
Do it, then feel awful about it later
Go ahead. Sometimes the greater good needs it
Make a sarcastic joke about it, then do it anyway

questions.text: Someone close to you has been acting strange lately. You...

options.text: Turn up with food, and stay until they talk
Write them a thoughtful note, and hope they open up
Check in quietly, without making a big deal of it
Lend them a book that changed your life

questions.text: You win an award at work. You...

options.text: Tell everyone, and put it where they'll all see it
Frame it, and hang it perfectly straight
Wonder what they're trying to distract you from
Give a short, gracious speech, then get back to work

questions.text: A friend asks for honest feedback on something they made. You...

options.text: Tell them the truth, kindly but clearly
Share a long reflection on creativity
Say it's good, then quietly fix it yourself
Find one thing to praise, and praise it a lot

questions.text: Big changes are coming at your workplace. You...

options.text: Wait and see. Change makes you nervous
Get everyone excited, and keep them on message
Throw yourself into it. You believe in the mission
Ask whether it comes with a pay rise

questions.text: Someone you love makes a choice you think is a mistake. You...

options.text: Say your piece once, then let them decide
Support them, and share some hard-won wisdom
Step in, and take charge of the whole thing
Stay polite, and keep your opinion to yourself

questions.text: Your company offers a procedure: you'll never remember work at home, or home at work. You...

options.text: Agree right away. Anything to stop thinking about the hard stuff
Refuse. Nobody's messing with your mind
Take it, if the perks are good
Trust the company. They know what's best
